## Summary

**Root cause of the retry bug:** `FilesService.Add` took a caller-built `io.Reader` + `contentType` and forwarded it straight to the transport. `http.NewRequestWithContext` only auto-populates `Request.GetBody` (needed to replay a request body) for `*bytes.Buffer`, `*bytes.Reader`, and `*strings.Reader`. A multipart body streamed from `os.Open` isn't one of those, so `GetBody` stayed nil, `canReplayBody` was false, and the retry transport (`pipedrive/retry.go`) refused to retry the 429 regardless of `RetryAllMethods` — exactly matching the report ("every other call retries fine" because JSON bodies get auto-boxed into `bytes.Reader` in `raw.go`).

**Fix:** Changed `FilesService.Add` (`pipedrive/v1/files.go`) to match the ergonomics already used by `CallLogsService.AddRecording` and product image uploads elsewhere in this SDK — it now takes `(ctx, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts...)` and builds the multipart body internally via the existing `internal/multipartbody.NewFile` helper. That helper fully encodes into a `*bytes.Reader`, which makes the request automatically replayable, so retries now work on 429/5xx without any extra caller-side wiring. This is a breaking signature change (documented in CHANGELOG.md under `[Unreleased]`), since it removes the manual-multipart escape hatch — no other code in the repo depended on it.

Added a regression test (`TestFilesService_Add_RetriesOnRateLimit`) that wraps the input reader to hide its concrete type (simulating an `*os.File`-like source) and confirms the request is retried on a 429. Updated `TestFilesService_Add` for the new signature. Full build and test suite pass.

Note: `FilesService.Update` has the same old `(body io.Reader, contentType string)` shape and the same latent retry issue, but the report only mentioned `Add`, so I left it untouched — let me know if you'd like that fixed too.
